detail.notes: two raised panels with deep multi-step moulded surrounds; large upper panel, shorter lower panel; wide flat stiles

notes: UNUSABLE for full-leaf geometry: the bottom of the leaf is below the frame of the photograph (image ends at y=1596 with plain door surface, no bottom rail, no floor). Leaf height, aspect and every height_h fraction are therefore unmeasurable and left null. Width IS reliable: left edge x=207 at the top drifting to x=224 at the image bottom, right edge x=880 to x=852; mid-height leaf width about 650 px. Roughly 3-5 percent of the leaf height is missing, so the 9-cell tone profile (measured over the visible span, top of leaf to y=1590) is very nearly the full profile but the last cell is a touch high. Squareness 0.87 is from the three visible edges only (L +0.64 deg, R -1.05 deg, T 0.0 deg); the bottom edge could not be included. HINGE SIDE IS ON THE RIGHT - the lever and cylinder sit near the LEFT edge, so inset_w is measured from the left (closing) edge. Extras: a horizontal turned brass pull rail across the middle of the leaf spanning u 0.33-0.72 with bosses at u 0.38 and u 0.62, at the same height as the cylinder. All hardware is brass, not the usual satin nickel. Strong top-to-bottom light falloff (contrast 2.84): the leaf reads #848E9E at the top and #2D3743 at the bottom, so the median #3B4859 is darker than the actual paint - the mid-height sample #5F6A7C is the better guide to the paint colour, hence the RAL 5014 pigeon-blue guess. A small blown-out white shield-shaped fitting sits on the leaf at about (255,105), unidentified. A beige bell push is on the wall to the right of the frame, not on the leaf. Leaf, gap and frame are all the same dark colour, so gap_w 0.08 is the whole shadowed reveal and cannot be separated from the frame face.
